qt: to the Commission Markus Buchheit (ID) Subject:
To coincide with President of the Commission Ms von der Leyen’s nomination as EPP’s lead candidate, the Commission’s DG Comm has just published 56 pages of propaganda trumpeting her achievements. 1.

How does this square with the Commission’s new Code of Conduct which states, in Article 10.5, that the Commission’s human and material resources must not be used for activities linked to the electoral campaign?
What legal consequences is it considering for this wrongful act?
Will Ms von der Leyen personally cover the production costs and personnel expenses incurred in putting together this illustrated brochure and sharing it online?
at: (English version) to the Commission Anna Fotyga (ECR) (4 March 2024) Subject: Inappropriate use of the Commission’s human and material resources in activities linked to an election campaign On 1 March 2024, a 56-page document entitled ‘Keeping our promise to Europe: The story of the von der Leyen Commission’ appeared on the Commission’s website. In an online post, one of the Commission staff involved in producing the document said: ‘Over the past few weeks, many great colleagues have dedicated long hours and weekends to bring all of this content together (…) it has been a gigantic team effort (…)’. (1) Meanwhile, the Code of Conduct for the Members of the European Commission states that the Commission’s President ‘may not use the Commission’s human or material resources for activities linked to the electoral campaign’ (2). Ursula von der Leyen is running for another five-year term as Commission President. Bearing in mind the very restrictive rules regarding MEPs’ assistants and their involvement in election campaigns: 1.

Is the involvement of Commission employees, both within and outside working hours, and of the Commission’s material resources in creating what is essentially an election campaign leaflet consistent with the above-mentioned provision of the Code of Conduct?

Will the Commission investigate this matter, and what does it expect the consequences to be for the unethical and illegal use of the Commission’s human and material resources for electoral purposes by a candidate for the position of Commission President in the 2024-2029 term?

to the Commission Markus Buchheit (ID) (13 March 2024) Subject: Use of the Commission’s material resources in the Commission President’s electoral campaign To coincide with President of the Commission Ms von der Leyen’s nomination as EPP’s lead candidate, the Commission’s DG Comm has just published 56 pages of propaganda trumpeting her achievements. 1. How does this square with the Commission’s new Code of Conduct which states, in Article 10.5, that the Commission’s human and material resources must not be used for activities linked to the electoral campaign? 2.
What legal consequences is it considering for this wrongful act?

3. Will Ms von der Leyen personally cover the production costs and personnel expenses incurred in putting together this illustrated brochure and sharing it online? Joint answer given by Vice-President Jourová on behalf of the European Commission (20 June 2024) The document mentioned by the Honourable Members in their questions is a publication of the Commission, which presents its achievements under the current mandate. It does not serve the purpose of any specific campaign, party or candidate. EU institutions have a responsibility to communicate about their activities to EU citizens and other interested parties . The Commission is appointed in the context of a democratic process following the European elections. It is therefore important to give account of its achievements to the citizens of the European Union as has been done in the past by previous Commissions (3).
